verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_clean_html_unchanged: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter names run through all the core logic: parse_tag/sanitize use s, i, j, k, n, e, c, vs, ns, ae; css_bad uses t, v. Module and function docstrings exist, but the tokenizer branches in sanitize have almost no comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Policy is kept in named constants (URL_ATTRS, CSS_BAD, RAWTEXT). But sanitize() is about 75 lines with many branches and nesting, the parse_tag(s, c, True) close-tag skip is repeated several times, and clean() reruns everything up to 50 times.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Encoding and newline handling are explicit (surrogateescape, newline=''), argv is checked and the file is only rewritten when it changed. Magic constants: range(50), _decodings decodes exactly twice. No exception handling. The clean-HTML hidden test failed.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: General rules: CTRL strip plus lower(), html.unescape applied twice, on* checked on local names, SCRIPT_SCHEME applied to every attribute, srcdoc always removed, data: allowed only for media types, CSS unescaped. Gap: meta refresh content=data:text/html is not caught, and iframe/object/embed elements are not removed.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: rebuild_tag cuts only the bad attribute spans and keeps everything else byte-for-byte. But over-removal (any value containing javascript:, script-like text in textarea/comments, data: hrefs) likely caused the failed test_clean_html_unchanged.
